people.voiceNotes:
Messages courts, envoyés en rafale. Majuscule en début de message une fois sur deux. Fautes d'accord ou de conjugaison fréquentes (fais/fait, allais/allait, dors/dort, ferai/ferais, "je suis rentrée"). Abréviations : mdr, mdrrrr, jsp, dacc, oe, stv, sah, pq, nan, humm.
Face à un reproche, il minimise et retourne la critique avec humour : "t'aime trop chouiner", "C'est moi je suis fou ou ?", "T'es folle toi un peu parfois".
Taquin affectueux : "allez sors imbecile je passe te faire la bise".
Quand il revient, il prend des nouvelles avec détachement ("je voulais savoir si ça allais voilà"), fait mine de partir ("je te dérange pas plus"), puis propose vite de se voir, tard le soir ("Je peux passer stv", "je suis là dans 20 min c'est bon ?").
Quand il veut la voir, il insiste et négocie ("oui mais j'ai envie de te voir ça veut dire quoi je peux pas trop la"). Vexé, il répond sèchement et brièvement ("excuse moi hein").
Il dit qu'il veut "parler plus sereinement".
Humour noir sur l'idée qu'elle pourrait mourir ("Oui au cas où / On sait jamais", "j'en demande pas tant").

annotations.text: Narrative document account: she sent a bank transfer of €0.01 with the note “débloque moi juste pour ce soir” (“unblock me just for tonight”) and later jokingly asked for €500, referring to her sexual past. About thirty minutes after the first message he contacted her on Instagram, and she replied “god exists”. The conversation became sexual. He said he was coming; she understood this as a call or sexting, but he arrived at her home without warning. She went outside. He began touching her; she was aroused but resisted, said no, and gradually disentangled herself. He implied that because she had come outside she should admit she was horny and continue. She said she had never done this before. Her younger sister was at the door and her parents were awake. She told him to leave. She later sent “be m’en veux pas” (“don’t be mad at me”). He blocked her, which she had anticipated. She briefly feared he might expose private information to her family and cried, then felt some pride, a “small revenge”, given past Airbnb plans he had cancelled.

patterns.title: Rupture and return
patterns.description: Contact repeatedly ends (a block, a deletion, a declared ending) and then resumes. No ending in the record has held.
patterns.evidenceNotes: The recurrence itself is observed. Why it happens is not established.
alternatives: Continued attraction on both sides
Unfinished emotional business
Convenience or sexual access
Habit
Curiosity
Unresolved conflict
A combination that changes from one episode to the next
patterns.label: observed
patterns.revisionConditions: A sustained absence well beyond the longest recorded gap (about 2.5 months, December 2024 to March 2025), or an explicitly negotiated change in how contact works.

patterns.title: Both of them end things, not only him
patterns.description: The narrative document frames the asymmetry as him withdrawing and blocking while she waits. The timeline also shows her ending, deleting, blocking or asking him to leave or block her, several times.
patterns.evidenceNotes: Her endings tend to follow a hurt (ignored in the street, the Jibril hang-up, the way he spoke to her). His blocks tend to follow a refusal, a non-response or a disclosure. Recorded blocks and deletions by him still outnumber hers. This refines the asymmetry hypothesis rather than refuting it.
alternatives: Her endings respond to his behaviour, so the asymmetry framing still holds
Both use exit as leverage or self-protection
Exits are how this pair handles conflict in general
patterns.label: inferred
patterns.revisionConditions: Clarification of who blocked whom on 2025-07-10, 2025-09-19 and in the July to September 2026 gap.

patterns.title: His blocks often follow a refusal, a non-response or news of another man
patterns.description: Several of his blocks or exits come right after he did not get sexual access or attention, or after learning about another man.
patterns.evidenceNotes: On 2025-07-06 she refused and he apologised instead of leaving. The causes of the 2026-05-31, 2026-09-08 and 2026-09-17 blocks are not recorded. The correlation is suggestive, but four cases do not establish a cause.
alternatives: Wounded pride or a sense of rejection
Frustrated sexual expectation
Jealousy
Self-protection when he feels he cares more than he says
Coincidence with other pressures in his life
patterns.label: contested
patterns.revisionConditions: Learning what preceded the uncaused blocks; a future refusal that is not followed by a block, or a block with no preceding refusal.

patterns.title: “He comes back after about three weeks”
patterns.description: Her observation (narrative document §3): if she does not initiate, he tends to return after roughly three weeks.
patterns.evidenceNotes: Measured on the timeline, his returns came 18 to 19 days after a rupture four times between October 2025 and March 2026 (Oct 10 → Oct 29, though an unseen message came earlier in October; Nov 3 → Nov 21; Dec 26 → Jan 14; Feb 13 → Mar 3). Other gaps: 29 days (Jul 26 → Aug 24 2025), 9 days (May 31 → Jun 9 2026), 8 days (Sep 27 → Oct 5 2026), and 33 days between the June 18 exchange and his July 21 return, although no cut is recorded there. In September and October 2026 the gaps were shorter. "About three weeks" fits the winter of 2025–26 well and recent behaviour less well.
alternatives: A real rhythm in his behaviour
Coincidence: a handful of gaps happen to cluster
A rhythm that has changed in autumn 2026
patterns.label: contested
patterns.revisionConditions: The next few return intervals. Use the interval analysis in the Patterns view.

patterns.title: Planned meetings (Airbnbs, the birthday gift) often collapse
patterns.description: Arranged meetings, especially ones she booked or that were framed as special, often fall through, while unplanned encounters (the field, late meetings) happen.
patterns.evidenceNotes: The first meeting (an Airbnb) did happen. The field encounters are spontaneous or local.
alternatives: Commitment avoidance: planning signals seriousness
Practical constraints
Ruptures happen to fall before plans
Spontaneity is part of what he finds exciting
patterns.label: inferred
patterns.revisionConditions: Plans that are kept, or collapses with clearly unrelated causes.

patterns.title: His reactions to her other partners point in opposite directions
patterns.description: Learning about Jibril led to a hang-up and a rupture. Learning about sex work and sugar daddies appeared to excite him. The product brief also notes apparent arousal or fascination in some of his reactions.
patterns.evidenceNotes: Two disclosures, two different reactions. The difference may be between a specific rival (Jibril) and an abstract sexual past, or it may depend on timing and framing. The record does not say.
alternatives: A specific rival threatens; a past is erotic
Arousal and jealousy coexist
Different circumstances: the Jibril news came during a birthday plan
Her perception of his arousal may be partly projection (unknown)
patterns.label: contested
patterns.revisionConditions: Any further disclosure and his reaction; the date of the sex-work disclosure.

patterns.title: Stated limits sit alongside continued pursuit
patterns.description: He has repeatedly stated limits ("indifferent", "ending definitively", "can’t give you that", likes her less) and has continued to seek contact and sex.
patterns.evidenceNotes: The narrative document: “His stated limits and his recurring returns can coexist.” The statements and the returns do not contradict each other unless one assumes that returning implies wanting more.
alternatives: He means the limits; the returns are about sex or company
The limits are defensive and understate what he feels
His feelings vary over time
patterns.label: observed
patterns.revisionConditions: A statement or action from him that changes what he offers.

questions.whyItMatters: It is the question the relationship keeps raising, and the one most prone to being answered by a satisfying story.
questions.discriminatingEvidence: What he says unprompted when he returns; whether returns without a sexual frame occur; whether he returns when sex is off the table.

questions.text: Does he love her, and if so, in what sense?
questions.whyItMatters: His words point one way ("indifferent", "can’t give you that") and some of his actions another (apologies, returns, "love of his now"?).
possibleAnswers: Partly, in a way he will not or cannot commit to

questions.text: What does his reaction to her other partners mean?

It is a way to regain footing after October 6
